newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Daiwa manager gets two months in prison.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Daiwa manager gets two months in prison.

text.p: A federal judge Friday sentenced the former general manager of the New York branch of Daiwa Bank Ltd. to two months in prison for helping to conceal $1.1 billion in trading losses at the bank from Federal authorities.
The former manager, Masahiro Tsuda, 54, was also fined $100,000, sentenced to one year of probation, and must post a $50,000 security bond.
Tsuda had pleaded guilty to the charge in April before U.S. District Judge Sidney H. Stein. The plea agreement provided that prosecutors drop a count of concealing a felony.

In February, Daiwa Bank pleaded guilty to charges of concealing the loss and agreed to pay $340 million in fines, the largest criminal fine levied against a financial institution in the United States.

The charges stem from the conduct of its top management during the summer of 1995, when managers deliberately covered up huge trading losses incurred by Toshihide Iguschi, an executive vice president at the New York branch.
Iguchi pleaded guilty to charges of doctoring bank records and embezzlement, stemming from the $1.1 billion in trading losses that he accumulated and covered up over 12 years.
